t: In a presidential democracy the people elect a president who heads the government for a fixed term and, unlike a prime minister, cannot be dismissed by the legislature for losing its support.
Devised by the framers of the Constitution of the United States in 1787, it rests on the separation of executive, legislative and judicial powers, each able to check the others.
It spread across Latin America in the 19th century; Juan Linz argued that its rigid terms and winner-takes-all elections endanger democracy, a view his critics dispute.
dyk: Under the original Constitution the runner-up in the electoral college became vice-president, so in 1796 John Adams found his chief rival, Thomas Jefferson, serving as his deputy; the Twelfth Amendment of 1804 ended the arrangement.
ev: The Constitution of the United States takes effect and George Washington is inaugurated as the first president
In Marbury v. Madison the Supreme Court asserts its power to strike down acts of Congress
Mexico’s first federal constitution creates a presidency on the American model
Brazil’s monarchy falls and Deodoro da Fonseca becomes the first president of a presidential republic
The Twenty-second Amendment limits American presidents to two terms
Chile’s armed forces overthrow President Salvador Allende, ending four decades of constitutional rule
Richard Nixon resigns as Congress moves to impeach him over the Watergate scandal
After mass protests, South Korea adopts a constitution with direct presidential elections

f.power: An elected president who is both head of state and head of government, checked by a separately elected legislature and an independent judiciary
f.legitimacy: A written constitution and the separate popular mandates of the president and the legislature
f.chosen: The president is elected by the people, directly or through an electoral college, for a fixed term, often with a limit on re-election; removal only by impeachment or for incapacity
f.examples: the United States (since 1789), the Republic of Chile (1932–1973), Costa Rica (since 1949), the Philippines (1946–1972), South Korea’s Sixth Republic (since 1987), Brazil’s New Republic (since 1985)
